transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Hello. I’m convinced I’ve made some terrible mistake in the books at work and that people are secretly watching everything I do, even though everyone keeps telling me it’s fine. My husband and my manager actually persuaded me to come here after I broke down in a meeting because I just can't trust my own judgment anymore.
Along with these worries, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I wake up every day with this heavy, sinking feeling of dread and emptiness in my chest that doesn't lift, even when good things happen. I've also completely lost interest in hiking and photography, which I used to love; now it all just feels pointless and exhausting, so I just cancel plans and sit on the couch.
Have you ever experienced these thoughts of being watched or making mistakes at a time when your mood was completely normal and you weren't feeling depressed?

No, I've never experienced anything like this when my mood was normal. Before this heavy depression started, I never had these paranoid thoughts or heard those voices at all. In fact, on the rare days when my mood lifts even a little bit, the feelings of being watched and the voice fade away completely.

Have you ever had periods lasting several days or more where you felt the exact opposite of depressed—such as having unusually high energy, feeling extremely 'high' or irritable, or needing very little sleep?
No, I've never had any periods like that. I've only ever felt these heavy, low feelings and constant exhaustion. I've never experienced having unusually high energy or feeling 'high'.
Have you ever had periods in the past, before this current struggle, where you felt this depressed, sad, or hopeless for weeks at a time?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This current struggle is the very first time in my life that I've felt this depressed or hopeless. It's all completely new to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is experiencing her first-ever severe depressive episode, characterized by persistent depressed mood, profound anhedonia, and constant exhaustion. This episode is accompanied by mood-congruent and mood-incongruent psychotic features, including persecutory delusions (believing she is being watched), delusions of guilt (convinced she made a terrible mistake at work despite reassurance), and auditory hallucinations (hearing voices). These psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the depressive state and resolve when her mood lifts. She has no history of prior depressive episodes, mania, or hypomania, which establishes the diagnosis of a Single Severe Depressive Episode with Psychotic Symptoms (F32.3).
